rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lead-in (L60): 'Ask Claude whether it met any of these.' Prompt opening: 'Did this session run into planning gaps, conflicting information, or other context in this repo that tripped the plan?' The verb differs (met / run into), but the noun-phrase referent carries over exactly — 'these' in the lead-in resolves to the three bullets (planning gaps, conflicting information, other context) immediately above, and the prompt spells out that identical list. Read in sequence the two feel like one continuous question, not two drafts — the rule's actual test ('place body lead-in's last sentence next to prompt's first sentence; share verb + noun-phrase? Rhyme → one move.'). This is the line closest to violating the rule in the file (the sibling pair three lines up, L38/L42, mirrors the verb exactly — 'whether these rules are auto-loaded' / 'are these rules auto-loaded' — so the new pair is measurably looser than the house standard right beside it), but the noun-phrase match keeps it inside the rule's intent. A tighter mirror ('Ask Claude whether this session ran into any of these.') was available and would remove the gap entirely; noted as a fix_hint, not a REVISE, since the current wording does not read as two drafts on an honest read.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Tighten the lead-in verb to echo the prompt's own ('ran into' instead of 'met') for a closer mirror, matching the sibling pair three lines above it — optional polish, not required.
